item.title: Becoming a Canadian Citizen on Canada Day
item.description: Every year on July 1st, people across the country come together to celebrate Canada Day. From fireworks at Niagara Falls to concerts, cultural events, and local gatherings in cities and towns across all provinces and territories. For some, this day has an even more personal meaning as it’s the day they officially become Canadian citizens.

item.title: The Warmest Cities in Canada
item.description: Canada is often associated with its cold climate, but many cities across the country are actually known for their warm climates year round. For newcomers searching for the warmest places to relocate, these cities and provinces provide a beautiful landscape along with a consistently mild climate.

item.title: How to find a job in Canada as a newcomer: The Ultimate Guide.
item.description: Canada is a land of opportunity, attracting people from all over the world with its vibrant culture, diverse landscapes, and strong economy. Whether you’re an international student, a visitor, or looking to work in Canada, this guide will help you navigate while searching for your first job.

item.title: Can I Go to Canada With a Felony or Criminal Record?
item.description: Are you worried that your old traffic ticket, misdemeanor or felony/DUI charge might make you criminally inadmissible to Canada? You are not alone. Use this comprehensive guide to understand how your past criminal history or a felony can affect your ability to enter Canada today.

item.title: Applying for an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) to Canada with a criminal record
item.description: Canada welcomes eligible foreigners for tourism, business, or family visits and has made this process quick and easy for those from visa-exempt countries with the Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) system.

item.title: Can Pilots or Flight Attendants go to Canada with a Criminal Record?
item.description: If you are a pilot or flight attendant, your career depends on being able to enter different countries smoothly. Having a single past criminal record can create serious obstacles that could limit or block your work.

item.title: Canada Study Permit Cap: Master’s and PhD Students Not Affected
item.description: Starting January 1, 2026, master’s and PhD students at public colleges and universities will not be included in the national study permit cap which was announced in Canada’s 2026-2028 levels plan.

item.title: Can I Travel to Canada for Work or Business with a DUI?
item.description: Canada and the United States share one of the world’s busiest borders, with countless people crossing every day for work, tourism, and trade.

item.title: What to Expect from Canada Immigration in 2026
item.description: Canadian immigration is already changing, with new policies and rule updates introduced earlier this year. It comes as no surprise that the start of a new year has brought changes in how people can come to Canada, stay in Canada, and become permanent residents or citizens.

item.title: How to Claim Canadian Citizenship by Descent Under Canada’s New Citizenship Act Bill C-3
item.description: Many people around the world may now qualify for Canadian citizenship because of recent changes to Canadian law. Bill C-3 corrects past citizenship rules and allows many individuals to reclaim citizenship that was previously lost or denied.
